methodology: Authorized runtime route and schema verification. HTTP method existence was primarily proven with unauthenticated GET/POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH requests that stop at Lucky authentication; method discovery does not execute protected mutating handlers. Selected GET routes were additionally verified with the repository OpenToken client. Request schemas were recovered from frontend pass-through/object literals and, where applicable, cross-checked against authorized read-only GET shapes. For nested-schema enrichment, current Lucky 3.0.0 frontend bundles were inspected only in memory and authorized GET responses were reduced to field names/JSON types; live domains, identifiers, paths, addresses and secret values were not persisted. Where frontend/read-only evidence was insufficient and the instance owner explicitly authorized it, selected routes used bounded API write probes against newly created disposable resources, followed by immediate cleanup and baseline verification; each such route records its exact boundary in schema_evidence. Dangerous/global operations were not exercised against existing business resources. For the six Docker legacy wrappers that lacked current UI call sites, upgrade/build used dedicated disposable BusyBox resources, Git/ZIP/import used validation-failure paths, and prune was exercised only by a temporary Lucky instance connected to a non-destructive mock Docker API. No real Docker prune handler reached the production Docker daemon.

same_bundle_prefix_artifacts.description: Literal-only paths that are strict prefixes of method-bearing routes from the same frontend bundle. Runtime probing confirmed no additional standalone method beyond already cataloged generic/template matches; PATCH probes were also 404. Suppression is version-bound and is not performed by the generic extractor.

webservice_reverseproxy_semantics.frontend_evidence: Lucky 3.0.0's shared WebService rule/subrule editor exposes NginxConf as a mini-nginx configuration field and documents proxy_set_header, proxy_hide_header, add_header, proxy_redirect, location and Lucky's path shorthand. The editor also exposes UseTargetHost, AutoProxyLocation, AutoProxyLocationWithoutSameHost, AddProtoToHeader/ProtoHeaderKey and AddRemoteIPToHeader/AddRemoteIPHeaderKey. The current frontend saves subrule edits by reading the complete parent WebService rule, changing DefaultProxy/ProxyList, and PUTing the preserved parent object back to /api/webservice/rule/{RuleKey}; copied/new subrules use an empty/unset Key and receive a Key from Lucky after persistence.

model.write_model: GET complete parent rule -> preserve unrelated fields -> edit/append DefaultProxy or ProxyList -> PUT complete parent rule; a newly appended subrule has no existing Key and Lucky assigns one

NginxConf.syntax: semicolon-terminated directives; # comments and quoted values with spaces are accepted

model.UseTargetHost: boolean; true sends the target URL host as the upstream Host header, false preserves the frontend request host
model.AutoProxyLocation: boolean; when enabled Lucky rewrites qualifying upstream redirects through a frontend lucky_auto_reverseproxy_<opaque-token>/ path
model.AutoProxyLocationWithoutSameHost: boolean; with AutoProxyLocation enabled, true leaves same-upstream-host redirects unchanged and rewrites redirects to a different host
model.AddProtoToHeader: boolean paired with ProtoHeaderKey; writes the client-side scheme into the configured upstream request header
model.AddRemoteIPToHeader: boolean paired with AddRemoteIPHeaderKey; writes the client address into the configured upstream request header
model.path_matching: Domains may include a frontend path prefix. Lucky removes that frontend prefix before location/path matching, then joins the remaining request path to any path already present in Locations; query parameters are preserved. $request_uri, $uri and $document_uri were observed with the frontend path still present.

webservice_reverseproxy_semantics.verification: On an authorized Lucky 3.0.0 production listener, a bounded probe added ten uniquely named TEST reverse-proxy subrules in one parent-rule PUT, exercised them through the existing TLS listener against an external echo/redirect origin, then removed only those TEST subrules from the latest parent rule. Runtime checks verified literal and variable proxy_set_header values, empty-value request-header removal, proxy_hide_header, add_header default status behavior and always, proxy_redirect for Location and Refresh, location prefix/exact/regex/case-insensitive-regex/negative matching, path wildcard/regexp/negative matching, frontend-prefix stripping plus upstream-base-path joining, query preservation, UseTargetHost, protocol/client-IP helper headers, AutoProxyLocation modes, and proxy_redirect off/default compatibility. The final business subrule list was byte-for-byte equal at the JSON-object level and no TEST subrule remained. Live hostnames, rule identifiers, client addresses and generated redirect tokens are intentionally omitted.

observations.add_header: without always it was present on 200 and absent on 418; with always it was present on both
observations.proxy_redirect: an explicit From/To mapping rewrote both Location and Refresh; proxy_redirect off preserved the raw redirect; proxy_redirect default was accepted and left both unrelated and same-upstream-host redirects raw in this probe
observations.auto_proxy_location: enabled mode rewrote both same-host and different-host redirects to a frontend /<prefix>/lucky_auto_reverseproxy_<opaque-token>/... path; AutoProxyLocationWithoutSameHost=true preserved same-host redirects while still rewriting different-host redirects
observations.connection_upgrade: $connection_upgrade expanded to upgrade for a request carrying Upgrade: websocket and Connection: Upgrade in the final verification run

webservice_reverseproxy_semantics.security: NginxConf is powerful configuration, not a safe template language. Do not interpolate untrusted user strings into directives. Parent-rule PUT is a whole-object replacement: re-read immediately before a write, preserve unknown/unrelated fields, minimize writes, and clean disposable probes by removing only their unique TEST-prefixed subrules from the latest object instead of restoring a stale snapshot.

webservice_sni_routing.frontend_evidence: Lucky 3.0.0 frontend service-type options expose the exact value SNIRouting; the SNI editor labels Locations as the SNI routing target address and requires parent-rule TLS.

webservice_sni_routing.verification: On an authorized production instance, a preserved WebService rule was updated with one new SNIRouting subrule, re-read successfully, and external TLS traffic matched by SNI was forwarded bidirectionally to a local TLS service. The target service presented the hostname certificate and completed an authenticated HTTPS CONNECT tunnel plus a read-only Git smart-HTTP ls-remote request. Unauthenticated proxy access returned 407 and an authenticated CONNECT to a non-allowlisted target returned 403. Live domain names, rule identifiers, addresses, ports and credentials are intentionally omitted.

ssl_certificate_mapping.verification: On an authorized Lucky 3.0.0 certificate managed by ACME, a disposable TEST certificate was created with MappingToPath already enabled before issuance. Lucky wrote non-empty <Remark>.key, <Remark>.crt and <Remark>.pem files into a unique TEST directory; the files were observed through Lucky's own local-path-browser API because the production Lucky runs in Docker and its /tmp namespace is not the host /tmp. Earlier bounded runs also showed that switching MappingToPath from false to true after an already-issued certificate did not immediately backfill old certificate material; mapping is tied to certificate material creation/change rather than a pure config toggle. Separate prior mapping verification found the mapped private key initially mode 0644 and reduced it to 0600 with MappingChangeScript configured to re-apply the restrictive mode. Certificate bodies, private keys, DNS API credentials, ACME account data and filesystem paths are intentionally omitted.

webdav_storage_behavior.security: The probe refuses to run when WebDAV is already active or has configured users, binds only loopback, disables firewall automation and TLS, uses a disposable random password, and never prints credentials or file content. GET /api/cron/dojobs successfully executed the task and the marker appeared through Lucky's local-path-browser.
